inputs.dilution_note: FY2026 diluted EPS equals basic EPS (28.38 cents) — zero dilutive employee share options outstanding at 31 March 2026 (300k dilutive options existed at FY2025, now nil). Shares held flat across all scenarios.
inputs.bank_debt_breakdown: Current bank loan $63k + non-current bank loan $1,029k = $1,092k
inputs.lease_treatment: Lease liabilities treated as operating, EXCLUDED from net debt per repo standard for NZ names. Lease principal repayments ($335k FY2026, per financing cash flow) are instead deducted directly from owner FCF each year (in projections, modelled as a % of revenue, ~1.2-1.4%).
inputs.net_debt_note: Net debt on BANK-DEBT-ONLY basis: $1,092k bank debt - $2,901k cash = -$1,809k (net cash position). This is the figure used in enterprise-to-equity bridge.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2026 OCF $4,026k - capex $196k (PP&E $83k + intangible development $113k) = $3,830k, as reported in Metrics.csv (company/repo definition).
inputs.last_fcf_note: Owner FCF = reported FCF ($3,830k) - lease principal repayments ($335k, financing-activity cash outflow under IFRS16 that is economically a cash operating cost for TAH's leased GP/ARC-admin premises). SBC and interest income adjustments considered but immaterial (see below) - NOT deducted.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report cash flow statement / equity reconciliation - SBC line shows -$37k, a forfeiture credit (an employee's share options were forfeited on departure), not an expense. TAH's ESOP is immaterial in absolute terms across the full history (peak $185k in FY2019, typically <$20k/yr since). No material SBC adjustment applied; sbc_pct_path held at 0.0% across the projection.
inputs.sbc_memo_value_if_noncash: Not applicable / trivial - SBC is negative (a credit) in FY2026 and has never exceeded 1% of revenue in any historical year. Treating it as cash vs non-cash changes owner FCF by less than $40k in any year, i.e. under 1 cent per share. This is structurally different from SBC-heavy tech names; no material valuation dependency on SBC treatment.
inputs.interest_income_treatment: NOT deducted from owner FCF. Net cash ($1,809k) is approximately 0.52x owner FCF ($3,495k) - well below the >1x materiality threshold in the workflow guidance - so interest income ($21k, trivial in dollar terms) is left inside FCF. Deducting it would change owner FCF by <0.6%.
inputs.nci_treatment: TAH's ARC subsidiaries are 70-80%-owned (Hub Aged Care, ARC Health, Cicada Health) plus other minority-owned GP entities. FY2026 NPAT of $3,091k includes $266k (8.61%) attributable to non-controlling interests (parent share: $2,825k). NCI balance-sheet carrying value is $457k. Because DCF enterprise value captures 100% of consolidated cash flow (all subsidiaries are fully consolidated), the NCI's proportionate economic claim (8.61%, based on the current profit-share ratio, held constant across the projection) is deducted from equity value before dividing by parent shares outstanding to avoid overstating the value attributable to TAH.NZ shareholders.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: FLAGGED: all headline CAGRs (revenue 26-33%, EPS 21-86%, FCF 20-73%) are massively inflated by four acquisitions in three years (EastMed/DFM FY23, Hub Aged Care FY24, ARC Health + Cicada Health Sept-2025) and cannot be used directly as the DCF growth driver. Equity CAGR (23-29%) is the most conservative headline figure but still includes acquired equity/goodwill, not organic compounding. Organic ARC enrolled-patient growth was only ~3.7% in H1 FY26 (ex the Sept-2025 acquisitions), and Community GP enrolled patients DECLINED 4.8% in FY26 (third consecutive year of decline). Selected base Y1 growth of 9.0% blends organic patient growth (~4-6%), the FY26 capitation uplift tailwind carrying into FY27, and a modest allowance for continuing bolt-on M&A (management has ruled out further Community GP deals but continues pursuing ARC bolt-ons), decelerating to a 4.5% Y5 rate as the business matures toward the ~3% demographic-driven terminal growth rate.
historical_growth.notes: SBC-adjusted FCF CAGR is not materially different from reported FCF CAGR here (68.2% vs 73.4% 3yr; 17.7% vs 19.8% 5yr) because SBC is negligible/negative at TAH - the modest gap reflects the lease-principal deduction only, not an SBC dilution signal. This contrasts with SBC-heavy US tech names where the adjusted/reported FCF CAGR gap is a red flag; here it is immaterial.

wacc_rationale: Base WACC of 14.5% (unchanged from prior 2026-06-25 DCF; re-validated against FY2026 actuals, no change to risk profile warranted). Constructed from: NZ small-cap base rate 11.5% (midpoint of 11-12% NZ small-cap range) plus structural risk premiums: (1) +1.0% single-payer funding concentration - effectively 100% of revenue flows from Health NZ/PHOs, which remains under Commissioner control amid a structural deficit; (2) +0.5% clinical workforce constraint - management's FY26 letter explicitly states ARC growth is capacity-constrained by clinician supply, not by demand, and cost of services rose to ~51% of revenue (from ~48%) as TAH paid up to secure coverage; (3) +1.0% micro-cap illiquidity - market cap ~NZD 44-49M through 2026, the Chairman disclosed a ~3x intra-year trading range (NZD 2.50-7.50) that he explicitly said reflects illiquidity rather than fundamentals; (4) +0.5% acquisition/minority-structure complexity - four acquisitions in ~2 years, four minority-owned subsidiaries (70-80% TAH-owned), deferred contingent consideration outstanding on two of them (ARC Health $280k, Cicada Health $219k, due Sept-2026). Total: 14.5%. Bull case 13.0% (assumes some risk-premium compression as scale increases toward $30-35M+ revenue and the capitation-formula reweighting proves durably favourable). Bear case 16.0% (escalated for funding freeze or accelerated workforce-driven margin/growth deterioration). No change from the prior DCF's WACC framework - FY2026 results (17.9% revenue growth, margin recovery to 20.8% EBITDA margin, continued bolt-on execution) do not materially change the underlying risk assessment.
valuation_philosophy: TAH.NZ is a NZX micro-cap healthcare compounder with a structurally attractive, non-discretionary niche (ARC medical services for an ageing NZ population, funded predominantly by government capitation) but a growth history that is almost entirely acquisition-driven and therefore not directly extrapolable. This model builds owner FCF from first principles each projection year (EBITDA margin -> D&A -> tax -> capex -> working-capital-on-growth -> lease principal) rather than carrying the FY2026 owner-FCF margin (15.5%) flat, because FY26's margin still embeds some one-off effects (deliberate ARC margin compression to secure clinician coverage, partially offset by the FY26 capitation uplift) and the mature margin trajectory needs to be built rather than assumed. A 5-year explicit horizon is used because the component build shows the Year-5 base-case owner-FCF margin (15.1%) is close to - not materially below - the FY2026 actual (15.5%), i.e. margins are not still ramping aggressively, so a 10-year extension is not required per the workflow's test. Lease principal payments (IFRS16, ~$335k FY2026) are deducted directly from owner FCF since they represent a real recurring cash outflow for TAH's leased GP-clinic and ARC-administration premises, while the corresponding lease liability is excluded from net debt (treated as an operating item, consistent with prior TAH.NZ modelling and general NZ-name treatment in this repo). SBC and interest income are both immaterial for TAH (SBC is a small negative/credit; net cash of $1.8M is under 1x the FCF base) and are therefore NOT adjusted, in contrast to SBC-heavy or cash-rich US tech names in this repo. Minority interests (NCI, 8.6% of FY2026 consolidated profit across four partly-owned subsidiaries) are deducted from equity value before arriving at parent intrinsic value per share, since 100% of consolidated cash flow is capitalised in the DCF but only ~91.4% belongs economically to TAH.NZ shareholders. The high 14.5% base WACC continues to reflect single-payer concentration, micro-cap illiquidity, and structural clinician-supply constraints - all directly evidenced in the FY26 Chairman's letter.

base.terminal_exit_multiple_basis: 10yr average historical EV/EBITDA (FY2021-FY2026, computed at FY-end prices)
base.description: Organic ARC enrolled-patient growth (~4-6%) plus continuing FY27 capitation-uplift tailwind plus a modest allowance for further ARC bolt-on acquisitions (management has ruled out further Community GP deals but continues pursuing ARC-focused M&A), decelerating from 9.0% to 4.5% as the FY27 'difficult operating environment' (management's own words) persists and the business matures toward the ~2.75% long-run demographic-driven terminal rate. EBITDA margin recovers gradually from the FY26-compressed 21.3% (deliberate trade-off to secure clinical coverage) toward 23.0% by Year 5 as the Digital Clinical Portal scales and newly-acquired ARC Health/Cicada Health integrate under TAWoW. D&A held near FY26's 4.74%-of-revenue actual. Capex stays asset-light (~0.9% of revenue). Working capital modelled as 15% capture of the YoY revenue increase (receivables/capitation timing). Cash tax rate held at the FY26 effective/statutory rate of ~28% (no valuation-allowance distortion to ramp away). Lease principal held at ~1.2% of revenue (slightly below FY26's 1.49%, reflecting the Belmont closure and no further Community GP lease expansion).

bull.description: New capitation formula (effective 1 July 2026, reweighted for age/multimorbidity/rurality) delivers a material and durable revenue-per-patient uplift for TAH's older, higher-acuity ARC population. ARC Health and Cicada Health integrate faster than base case, accelerating Canterbury/Bay of Plenty growth. NP Development Programme graduates ease the binding clinical-workforce constraint, allowing 1-2 additional ARC bolt-on acquisitions per year at TAH's demonstrated low entry multiples. Digital Clinical Portal drives real operating leverage, lifting EBITDA margin to 25.2% by Year 5. Some risk-premium compression (WACC 13.0%) as the business scales past $30-35M revenue and demonstrates funding-model resilience.

bear.description: Health NZ funding constraint tightens post the FY26 uplift; the July-2026 capitation reweighting proves neutral-to-negative in practice. Community GP enrolled-patient attrition continues for a fourth-plus consecutive year, potentially forcing further small-practice closures (as with Belmont) and EastMed goodwill impairment. Clinical workforce shortage deepens, capping ARC organic growth near 1.5-4% and forcing continued clinician wage inflation that compresses EBITDA margin toward 19.2% (below even the FY26-compressed level). No further acquisitions completed. Small-cap risk premium rises (WACC 16.0%) as macro/funding uncertainty increases.

base.implied_exit_multiple_note: 8.74x Year-5 FCF (Gordon-implied). On an EV/EBITDA basis this is well below the historical 10-year average (10.59x) and below current EV/EBITDA (~7.4x at current price is close; see sanity check), so the model does NOT assume multiple expansion.

entry_price.note: Entry price sits modestly below intrinsic value in every scenario (base $3.22 vs IV $3.28; bull $4.46 vs IV $4.80; bear $2.19 vs IV $2.12-note bear entry is essentially at IV because bear growth (1.5-4%) is far below the 15% hurdle, so nearly no premium is paid for growth). This is the expected sanity property given base/bear growth rates (4.5-9% and 1.5-4% respectively) sit well below the 15% hurdle rate.

sensitivity.matrix_note: Rows = WACC (ascending 12.5%-16.5%), Columns = Terminal Growth (ascending 1.75%-3.75%). Base case is row 3, col 3 ($3.28). Built on base-case FCF path and EBITDA-based exit-multiple cap (10.59x); Gordon growth binds throughout this sensitivity range so the cap does not constrain any cell.

sanity_check.result: PASS. Base-case IV of $3.28 implies an EV/EBITDA of 5.37x, P/E of 11.56x, P/B of 5.93x and P/Sales of 1.45x on FY2026 actuals - all BELOW their respective historical averages (EV/EBITDA avg 10.59x, P/E avg ex-outlier 17.83x, P/B avg 8.51x, P/S avg 2.54x) and comfortably within (in fact below) the historical minimum-to-maximum ranges. No trip rules fired. The current market price of $4.47 (EV/EBITDA 7.43x, P/E 15.75x, P/B 8.08x, P/S 1.98x) sits close to the historical average multiples and well above the base-case DCF fair value, implying the market is pricing in continued strong execution (closer to the bull-case trajectory) rather than the base-case deceleration this model assumes.
key_observations: All historical growth CAGRs (revenue, EPS, FCF, even equity) are acquisition-distorted; none used directly as the DCF growth driver.
FY2023 P/E of 36.45x is an acquisition-cost-driven earnings trough, excluded from P/E averages but retained in the table for transparency.

TAH's structurally high ROE (~56% TTM) against thin book equity means P/B will always look elevated versus 'normal' companies; the correct test is against TAH's own historical P/B range, not an absolute P/B threshold, and the base IV passes comfortably below even the historical minimum.

Current price ($4.47) sits between the base-case IV ($3.28) and bull-case IV ($4.80), i.e. the market is pricing something close to the bull scenario - continued capitation-formula tailwind, successful ARC Health/Cicada Health integration, and further accretive bolt-ons.

The 14.5% base WACC (single-payer concentration + micro-cap illiquidity + workforce constraint + acquisition complexity) is the primary driver pulling base IV below the current price; this is an intentional, evidence-based structural discount, not a modelling error.

investment_summary.conclusion: At $4.47, TAH.NZ trades above base-case intrinsic value ($3.28, -26.6% implied downside) and even above the probability-weighted IV ($3.37, -24.6%), sitting between the base and bull-case ($4.80) fair values. The FY2026 audited results were genuinely strong (revenue +17.9%, EBITDA margin recovery to 20.8%, NPAT +24.7%, ROE 55.9% TTM) and the July-2026 capitation-formula reweighting and continuing ARC bolt-on pipeline are real, evidenced tailwinds - but management's own FY26 letter explicitly frames FY27 as a 'difficult' operating environment with 'no near-term relief' from workforce shortages and cost pressures, and Community GP enrolled patients have now declined for three consecutive years (with the forced Belmont closure underscoring small-practice fragility). All historical growth CAGRs are acquisition-inflated noise; this model instead builds owner FCF bottom-up from an EBITDA margin that only gradually recovers from FY26's deliberately-compressed level, with lease principal payments deducted as a genuine recurring cash cost and 8.6% of value ceded to non-controlling interests across TAH's four partly-owned subsidiaries. The bull case ($4.80, +7.5%) is very close to the current price, meaning the market is effectively already pricing a favourable resolution of the capitation-reweighting catalyst and successful further M&A execution. The bear case ($2.12, -52.5%) reflects a genuine and disclosed risk - Health NZ fiscal pressure and structural clinician shortage are not hypothetical, they are the company's own stated primary operational risks. An investor seeking a 15% IRR would need a base-case entry price of $3.22 (28% below current) or better; only the bull scenario's entry price ($4.46) sits near the current quote. TAH remains a high-quality, structurally-advantaged NZ demographic-compounder, but at $4.47 it is priced for sustained bull-case execution rather than the base-case deceleration this model - anchored in management's own cautious FY27 guidance - considers most likely.
